item.title: 0.6.1-beta.4
item.description:
Aki 0.6.1-beta.4

New

  • Support Aki and Check for Updates at the foot of the Settings sidebar, above Quit.

Changed

  • Right-clicking a session's ring shows only what you can do with that session. Hiding the sidebar, settings and quitting are in the Aki submenu at the end; an open card closes when the menu opens, and no other card opens while it is up.

Fixed

  • Connect said “Failed” for Claude Code when it was installed with its own installer.

item.title: 0.6.1-beta.2
item.description:
Aki 0.6.1-beta.2

Changed

  • Right-clicking a session's ring shows only what you can do with that session. Hiding the sidebar, settings and quitting are in the Aki submenu at the end.
  • An open card (or the "+N" list) closes when that menu opens.

Aki 0.6.0

Use it your way, and clear the screenshots

  • Get started asks how you'll use Aki: only your week (limits and cost, no permissions needed), only pointing at things for your agents, or both. Change it any time in Appearance → Use Aki for.
  • Screenshots piling up (Get started and Storage): Aki counts the Mac's screenshots on the Desktop, in Downloads and in your screenshot folder, and moves the ones older than 7, 30 or 90 days to the Trash in one click. Nothing is deleted for good.

Aki 0.5.0

Your week at a glance

  • A ring for Claude and one for Codex at the end of the sidebar: how much of the weekly limit is used and how much of today's share, in colour (green, yellow from 50%, orange from 70%, red from 90%).
  • Hover a ring: when each window renews, whether you're over or under the pace, today's tokens and what they'd cost at API prices, the last 7 days and the projects that used most.
  • Settings → Show in the sidebar: sessions and limits, only limits (a usage meter) or only sessions.
  • aki usage prints it in the terminal.
  • Read from Claude Code's and Codex's own logs on your Mac — only the token counts, never the conversations.

Aki 0.4.4

  • The right session, by itself: marking starts on the agent tab you're in, or were in a moment ago, before the page's port.
  • ⌘Z undoes the last mark.
  • Space held while dragging moves the whole area, as the Mac's ⌘⇧4.
  • ⇧ in the middle of a drag no longer gets in the way.
